regress-563221.shape: eval of a never-called function whose else-block holds 10,000 `e;` statements
regress-563221.cause: Each `e;` lowers to getIdentifierValue(scope, 'e', ...) plus a completion store. Codegen emits about 100 instructions per site: a surface call with descriptor/signature checks and about 60 frame-slot loads/stores (no register allocation). 10,000 sites exceed maxScriptCodeBytes (2 MiB), so compile fails cleanly as unsupported.
regress-563221.blocker: Needs about 3x smaller per-site code (A3: register allocation/liveness, already queued) or lazy compilation of nested function bodies in runtime-compiled entries (proposed to P in handoff-H-to-P.md, awaiting agreement; touches P's eval/Function compile path).

regress-610026.shape: eval of 2^21 sequential empty blocks (4 Mi chars), then about 2^22, then that plus one
regress-610026.cause: Managed-heap exhaustion during the native parse. Each empty block costs about 1-2 KB of transient memory (block node plus its own statement list; an empty statement costs far less), and the parser retains every token for backtracking. The full test reads about 12M tokens and 6M blocks.
regress-610026.lowering: Blocks without declarations already create no environment and only 13.8 KB of code at any count. A further lowering change that drops them from the lowered module (saved as .tint-bootstrap/regress-empty-block-lowering-h-v1.patch) does not change the native outcome, so it is not proposed alone.
regress-610026.blocker: Needs a parser redesign: a streaming token window trimmed below the earliest live backtrack mark, plus no node for empty blocks in statement lists (after the directive prologue). Even the planned 512 MiB heap cannot hold about 12M retained tokens. H can implement it on request, but it touches the shared TypeScript/JavaScript parser.
